unit.can_do_en: pick up a parcel and spell my name.

brief.situation_en: Maria picks up a parcel. Jonna works at the counter.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Hi! I've come to pick up a parcel.

judge.reason: Same: I came to pick up a package; only register differences.

lines.speaker: Jonna
lines.gloss_en: OK. Do you have the tracking code?

judge.reason: Same question about having a tracking code; okei/selvä and onks/onko are register differences.
'Joo' is the spoken equivalent of 'kyllä'; the rest is identical (in this phone).
Same: what is your last name; only register differences.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Silva. Äs, ii, äl, vee, aa.
lines.text_kirja: Silva. S, I, L, V, A.
lines.gloss_en: Silva. S, I, L, V, A.

judge.reason: Both spell the name S-I-L-V-A; the spoken version writes out the Finnish letter names phonetically, which is only a difference in register/notation.

puhe.text: Silva. Äs, ii, äl, vee, aa.

kirja.text: Silva. S, I, L, V, A.

judge.reason: Same: here is my driver's license; mun/minun and ajokortti/ajokorttini are register differences.
Same: here is your package; only register differences.

forms.why_en: Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Adds -i for the past and -n for 'I': tulla becomes tulin.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to fetch, to pick up, to apply
forms.why_en: After tulla 'to come', the verb takes -maan: hakemaan. Speech says hakee.
The partitive singular after hakemaan: paketti becomes pakettia. Speech says pakettii.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: On with -ko to ask a question. Speech often says -ks: onks.
Sinä with -lla. With on it means 'you have'. Speech shortens it to sul.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Joo is the everyday spoken yes. Books write kyllä.
Tämä, this, with -ssä for 'in': tässä. Said when handing something over.
Adds -ssa for 'in, on': puhelin becomes puhelimessa, the n turning to me.
Kiitti is the everyday spoken thanks. Books write kiitos.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Sinä with -n for 'your': sinun. Speech shortens it to sun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for your
forms.why_en: Adds -si for 'your'; sukunimi turns its i to e first: sukunimesi. Speech says sun sukunimi.
The form of olla, to be, for he, she or it. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Minä with -n: minun pitää means I have to. Speech shortens it to mun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for my
forms.why_en: Adds -ni for 'my': ajokortti becomes ajokorttini. Speech just says mun ajokortti.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for your
forms.why_en: Adds -si for 'your': paketti becomes pakettisi. Speech just says sun paketti.
